title: Poled-fibre phase modulator for efficient high-dimensional quantum measurements
authors: Nayda Guerrero, Nelson Villalba, Gustavo H. dos Santos, Carlos J. Salazar, Cristobal Melo, Fernando Castillo, Jaime Cariñe, Guilherme B. Xavier, Esteban S. Gómez, Stephen P. Walborn, João Pereira, Gabriel Saavedra, Gustavo Lima
abstract: Efficient detection of quantum states underpins advanced device-independent quantum-information protocols that provide the ultimate level of security for tasks including quantum random number generation and quantum key distribution (QKD). High-dimensional encoding is a natural route to boost the performance of such protocols, offering enhanced noise resilience and higher information capacity, yet their practical implementation remains challenging. A key experimental bottleneck in higher dimensions is the typical need of active modulators for basis selection, which incur substantial optical losses and polarization-sensitive operation. Poled optical fiber phase modulators (PFPMs) are a fiber-native electro-optic technology that naturally addresses these challenges, combining sub-dB insertion loss, intrinsic polarization independence, and direct compatibility with standard telecommunications fiber. Here we report the first use of a PFPM for active quantum-state measurements in a fully fiber-integrated platform. Basis selection in our receiver for four-dimensional qudits is achieved using a single PFPM, substantially simplifying the receiver architecture. As a benchmark, we perform a four-dimensional QKD session and obtain a finite secret-key rate per pulse that, to the best of our knowledge, surpasses all previously reported QKD demonstrations. Our results establish poled-fiber electro-optic modulation as a broadly applicable platform for high-efficiency detection in fiber-integrated quantum information processing.
summary: This paper demonstrates the use of Poled-fibre phase modulators (PFPMs) to overcome major bottlenecks in high-dimensional quantum measurements. By offering low loss and polarization independence directly on standard telecom fibers, PFPMs enable a highly efficient receiver for advanced QKD protocols. The results establish this technology as a key building block for scalable, fiber-integrated quantum information processing.
main_problem: The primary challenge is achieving efficient, high-dimensional quantum state detection for advanced protocols like QKD, where conventional modulators introduce significant optical losses and polarization sensitivity.
main_result: The use of Poled-fibre phase modulators (PFPMs) enables a fully fiber-integrated platform that significantly reduces receiver loss and achieves record finite secret-key rates in four-dimensional QKD demonstrations.
method: The authors implemented an active quantum measurement basis selection using the PFPM within a high-dimensional QKD setup, comparing its performance against traditional $	ext{LiNbO}_3$ modulators.
model_or_system: The system utilizes Poled-fibre phase modulators (PFPMs) integrated into a fiber platform for active quantum state measurements in four dimensions ($d=4$). This technology is inherently compatible with standard telecom fibers and offers low loss and polarization independence.
key_observables: Finite secret-key rate per pulse, receiver insertion loss (e.g., 2.79 dB vs 5.76 dB), and the ability to perform basis switching using a single modulator.
important_parameters: Four-dimensional qudits ($d=4$), sub-dB insertion loss, $10 	ext{ dB}$ channel attenuation, and operational stability up to $100 	ext{ kHz}$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the mode-dependent loss contribution to QBER is negligible compared to the measured baseline interferometric QBER.
figures_summary: Figures compare receiver losses using conventional modulators versus PFPMs for basis selection; other figures detail characterization setups and system cross-sections.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the need for low-loss, high-dimensional measurement devices. It then details the fabrication and characterization of the PFPM. Finally, it presents experimental results demonstrating its use in a four-dimensional QKD session, quantifying performance improvements over prior art.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics and photonic QI as it provides an ultra-low-loss, fiber-native component crucial for scaling up complex quantum network protocols beyond laboratory settings.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Effect of receiver loss in quantum photonic experiments. Top: a conventional receiver based on a commercial, fiber-pigtailed LiNbO3 phase modulator (3 dB insertion loss) implements the basis-selection unitary U, pushing the overall measurement efficiency below the threshold required for DI quantum information experiments or severe limiting the rate attainable in QKD. Bottom: a receiver based on a poled-fiber phase modulator implements the same unitary at sub-dB insertion loss, constituting the architecture demonstrated in this work.

Figure 4. Schematics of the four-dimensional HD-QKD system used. A weak coherent pulse is distributed among four single- mode fibers through a four core multicore beam splitter (4C-MBS) [32] and sent to the Preparation Stage, where four LiNbO3 phase-modulators generate the QKD qudit states. The photons are then multiplexed into a 520 m spool of a 4C multicore fiber, which constitutes the transmission channel. At Bob, the photons are routed to the high-efficiency detection system, within which a single PFPM (yellow Basis Selection box) realises the active basis switching.
